cohort: 315 women with singleton pregnancy who were undergoing labor induction at term
finding: Women who achieved vaginal delivery had steeper slopes of parasagittal angle of progression and head-perineum distance against fetal head station and cervical dilation than those who achieved cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The study used transperineal ultrasound to assess fetal head descent during labor and found differences in labor progress between women who had vaginal deliveries and those who had cesarean deliveries.
